reason: This passage describes the Exodus crossing of the Red Sea, centered on God's divine power and judgment rather than compassion as a leadership model. Key elements include: (1) God explicitly hardening Pharaoh's heart (וַחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת־ לֵב־ פַּרְעֹה) to orchestrate the confrontation; (2) the complete destruction of the Egyptian army with no survivors (לֹֽא־ נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד־ אֶחָֽד - 'not one remained'); (3) God's stated purpose being self-glorification (וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה - 'I will be glorified in Pharaoh'); and (4) the use of overwhelming force and divine power to achieve objectives. While the Israelites are delivered, this is presented as salvation and deliverance through power, not as a demonstration that compassion is the model for good leadership. The passage exemplifies leadership through absolute authority, strategic might, and divine judgment rather than compassion for people.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
